feedback-sbi.title: Situation-Behavior-Impact feedback
points: Describe the specific situation (when and where), the observable behavior, and its impact.
Stick to facts the other person would agree happened; avoid labels like 'unreliable'.
After stating the impact, pause and invite their view before proposing solutions.

open-questions.title: Open questions and active listening
points: Open questions start with what, how, or walk me through; they can't be answered yes or no.
Reflect back what you heard in your own words before moving on.
Follow-up questions that reuse the other person's words show you listened.

commitments.title: Closing with clear commitments
points: A good close names the action, the owner, and the date.
Ask the other person to restate the agreement, or restate it yourself and confirm.
Offer a check-in point so the commitment has a natural follow-up.

negotiation-anchoring.title: Anchoring a counteroffer
points: Lead with enthusiasm for the role, then make a specific numeric ask.
Back the number with one or two reasons: market data, competing offers, or scope.
After stating the number, stop talking and let the other side respond.

negotiation-levers.title: Negotiating beyond base salary
points: If base is constrained, ask what flexibility exists elsewhere.
Common levers: signing bonus, an early compensation review, start date, or development budget.
Get any agreed terms confirmed in writing.

deescalation.title: De-escalating an upset stakeholder
points: Let them finish; interrupting increases frustration.
Name the emotion and the impact before explaining causes.
Keep explanations short and non-technical, then pivot to the plan.

apology-ownership.title: Apologizing with ownership
points: Apologize for the specific impact, not 'any inconvenience'.
Avoid shifting blame to other teams, vendors, or the client.
Pair the apology with what is changing so it doesn't happen again.
